title: Operator Clearance Observer Tool Discovery Mismatch
summary: Record the post-restart tool discovery result for FP-MCP-220. The MCP bridge service was restarted by the operator and the running process was observed using /home/ridasaidd/forgepilot-chatgpt-mcp/dist/server.js with cwd /home/ridasaidd/forgepilot-chatgpt-mcp. The checkout is clean at MCP bridge commit 02ce465 and dist/server.js contains the new forgepilot_get_operator_local_execution_clearance_status registration. However, ChatGPT tool discovery still does not expose that new observer tool. This is recorded as a tool-manifest/discovery mismatch, not an implementation failure and not an execution event.
caveats: systemctl --user cat could not be read from the MCP terminal context because the user bus was unavailable there, but the process command line and cwd were observed directly through /proc and ps.
The new observer exists in source and compiled dist output and pnpm build previously passed.
The observer could not be called through ChatGPT because the tool is not exposed in the active tool manifest.
No local clearance artifact was created.
No approval was consumed, no disable switch was cleared, no runner start endpoint was contacted, no OpenCode process was started, and FP-027 did not run.

toolDiscoveryObservation.inference: Likely ChatGPT-side tool manifest/cache or connector discovery mismatch after service restart, because the running process path and compiled dist output match the updated implementation.

recommendedNextActions: Refresh/reconnect ChatGPT connector/tool session again or start a new ChatGPT session so the tool manifest is rebuilt.
After the observer appears in tool discovery, call it once in read-only mode with current scoped inputs and record the result.
Do not wire execution enablement or consume approval until the observer is callable through the MCP surface and passes its own fail-closed behavior.
